name: What should be included in a custom cabinetry quote?

mainEntity.name: What details do homeowners need to compare bids fairly for custom cabinets and finish work?
mainEntity.text: What details do homeowners need to compare bids fairly for custom cabinets and finish work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Comparing cabinetry quotes is difficult when one shop includes more scope than another. A complete quote should clearly state the cabinet construction method, substrate, door style, finish type, hardware brand or allowance, installation scope, and any assumptions about wall conditions or site readiness. It should also identify whether the price includes design drawings, field measurements, finish samples, delivery, protection during install, and final punch-list work. If the project includes custom paint matching, glazing, integrated lighting, or appliance panels, those items should be spelled out separately. Ask what is excluded as well, because omissions can become surprise costs later. The best bid is not the cheapest one; it is the most complete and easiest to compare. If two proposals look similar in price but one leaves out prep or finish touch-up, the true cost may be very different.
acceptedAnswer.description: A proper custom cabinetry quote should list cabinet construction, materials, finish system, hardware, installation, site measuring, design revisions, and any exclusions. It should also specify whether sample approval, delivery, touch-up work, and cleanup are included. Without those details, two quotes are not directly comparable.
